headline: High: Chatwoot’s broad egress and customer-data handling create default leakage/compliance risk; Botpress adds only limited write-side conflict risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, Botpress is a chatbot platform and Chatwoot exposes integrations and message flows, so if operators bridge them via copy-paste or shared workspace, attacker-controlled text could cross from Chatwoot into Botpress. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF operators manually copy Chatwoot messages into Botpress prompts
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two agents
mitigations: Disable any manual relay of raw customer text
Add a provenance label to all imported messages
Restrict Botpress to templated prompts only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware
requires-engineering: separate the agents onto isolated workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, messages, and reports, while Botpress has network egress set to none. A shared workspace is not documented, but if one is introduced, Chatwoot’s data could be exposed through Botpress outputs or logs. The interaction is inferred from the profiles, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem or workspace
IF Botpress is configured to ingest Chatwoot-exported files or transcripts
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and mounts
Do not place customer exports in Botpress-readable paths
Redact customer identifiers before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage ACLs
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while Chatwoot has broad network egress and API integrations, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same mutable resource. Without a shared directory, database, or git state, the conflict pathway is limited. If a shared mutable target is added, contention becomes more relevant.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or repository
IF either agent is connected to the same mutable database or OAuth scope
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories
Assign separate service accounts
Freeze package installs during shared runs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources
requires-engineering: split mutable state per agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot’s integrations and customer-support workflows can act on content, while Botpress is a chatbot that can generate responses or structured text. If Chatwoot consumes Botpress output without verification, a mistaken Botpress answer can cascade into customer-facing actions or replies. The profiles do not prove this default path, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF Chatwoot treats Botpress output as authoritative
IF Botpress-generated text is forwarded into customer replies or automation
mitigations: Insert human review before outbound actions
Require schema validation on Botpress outputs
Limit Botpress to draft-only responses
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before actioning
requires-engineering: log and diff all downstream edits

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot explicitly touches customer data and related records, while Botpress is an open-source chatbot with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. If regulated customer data flows from Chatwoot into Botpress, the pair can create a compliance breach by default unless operators add controls. Uncertainty about Botpress’s controls escalates this to high.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed from Chatwoot into Botpress
IF Botpress is deployed without documented retention and residency controls
mitigations: Block regulated data from Botpress inputs
Add a data-classification gate before transfer
Document retention and deletion handling
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations
